titulo: Verbs in the present tense and sentence order: The regular present tense

aula.titulo: Verbs in the present tense and sentence order
aula.objetivo: Conjugate regular verbs in the present tense, put the verb in second position and make simple questions and negations.

blocos.texto: Goal of the lesson. By the end of the four sessions, you build affirmative sentences with the verb always in the right place, even when you start the sentence with heute, jetzt or hier.

blocos.contexto: Tom and Camila plan the evening in the hostel kitchen.

linhas.ru: — Heute koche ich. Du kochst morgen.
linhas.en: — Today I cook. You cook tomorrow.
linhas.audio: Heute koche ich. Du kochst morgen.

linhas.ru: — Gern! Jetzt lerne ich noch Deutsch.
linhas.en: — Gladly! Right now I am still studying German.
linhas.audio: Gern! Jetzt lerne ich noch Deutsch.

linhas.en: — Then we will have tea later.

linhas.ru: — Ja, gern. Hier trinkt man abends oft Tee, oder?
linhas.en: — Yes, gladly. Here people often drink tea in the evening, right?
linhas.audio: Ja, gern. Hier trinkt man abends oft Tee, oder?

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: count the positions. One block, then the verb. Always in that order.
blocos.comparacao: In English the subject stays right in front of the verb, even after a time word: “Today I live in Munich.” The same order in German gives Heute ich wohne in München, which is wrong. In German, the verb never leaves the second position. When something other than the subject opens the sentence, the subject goes after the verb.

blocos.titulo: The regular present tense: stem + ending
blocos.explicacao: Almost all German verbs end in -en in the infinitive. Remove the -en to find the stem and add the endings: -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en. If the stem ends in -t or -d (arbeiten, finden), an -e- is inserted before -st and before -t, to make pronunciation easier: du arbeitest, er arbeitet. If the stem ends in -s, -ß or -z (heißen, reisen), the «du» loses the -s of the ending: du heißt, du reist. The forms «wir», «sie» and «Sie» are the same as the infinitive.
blocos.comparacao: In English the verb hardly changes («I speak, you speak, we speak») except for the «-s» of «he / she / it speaks». German has more endings than that, but only five different ones, and «wir», «sie» and «Sie» repeat the infinitive.

erros.motivo: Stem in -t: an -e- is inserted before the -st.
Stem in -s: the «du» loses the -s of the ending.

blocos.enunciado: Diga: «Ich wohne in … Ich arbeite … Ich lerne Deutsch. Du lernst auch Deutsch.»
Write the 6 forms of «sein» from memory.
